fact_check.claim: Minimum of 8 courses to cover all 10 distribution categories
fact_check.note: Page: 'Students must complete a minimum of 8 courses to fulfill all 10 distribution categories below.'

fact_check.claim: Up to two courses may count for two distribution requirements; faculty can list a course under up to two categories
fact_check.note: Chronicle: 'they may count up to two courses as satisfying two distribution requirements at once'; 'faculty can list courses for up to two distribution categories rather than one.'

fact_check.claim: Distribution courses can be taken S/U if not also used for a major or minor requirement
fact_check.note: Matches page wording.

fact_check.claim: S/U limit worded as courses counting toward major requirements or serving as major admission prerequisites; S/U courses can still fulfill distribution
fact_check.note: Page: cannot 'also count toward major requirements or serve as prerequisites for admission to the major'; S/U can still satisfy distribution.

fact_check.claim: Students who matriculate in fall 2020 or after follow the current curriculum
fact_check.note: Page says exactly this.

fact_check.claim: Ten category names and codes (ALC, BIO, ETM, GLC, HST, PHS, SCD, SSC, SDS, SMR -AS)
fact_check.note: All ten names with codes appear on the page.

fact_check.claim: A course counts only if its code ends in -AS
fact_check.note: Page: without '-AS' the course will not fulfill a distribution requirement.

fact_check.claim: 8 semesters to fulfill the requirements
fact_check.note: Page: 'You have 8 semesters to fulfill these requirements.'

fact_check.claim: DUST report is updated after each semester and shows progress
fact_check.note: Page says updated after each semester to reflect progress.

fact_check.claim: Class Roster searchable by subject, instructor and credits
fact_check.note: Page lists subject, class year, college, time offered, instructor, credits.

fact_check.claim: Add a regular course in the first 15 calendar days, except courses with special deadlines
fact_check.note: Page includes the exception for specific courses with special deadlines.

fact_check.claim: Drop without transcript record in first 57 days; later withdrawal shows a W
fact_check.note: Matches page.

fact_check.claim: Courses with overlapping content cannot both count toward the degree
fact_check.note: Page says this.

fact_check.claim: Transfer students need at least 60 academic credits at Cornell and at least four semesters in residence
fact_check.note: Page: 'at least four semesters in residence and complete at least 60 academic credits at Cornell.'

fact_check.claim: AP, IB or A-Level scores do not fulfill the language requirement
fact_check.note: Page: 'No. These scores may be used for placement... will not fulfill the requirement.'

fact_check.claim: Degree page links each category to the current term's Class Roster results (e.g. 'Fall '26 ALC-AS courses')
fact_check.note: Each category has a 'Fall '26' roster link.

fact_check.claim: 2018 plan called for five different categories within the first four semesters; current degree page does not repeat it
fact_check.note: News page: 'Students will fulfill five different distribution categories in their first four semesters'; degree page has no such rule.

fact_check.claim: Catalog link is the official per-category course list
fact_check.note: Page returned empty content to our fetcher; a web search result titles it 'College of Arts and Sciences Distribution Requirement Course List' with courses organized by area, so the description is plausible.

fact_check.claim: ETM-AS: cognition, language, reasoning and how ethical values are formed, drawing on psychology, linguistics or philosophy
fact_check.note: Page says 'investigate the human mind and its capacities' and that ethics courses explore 'the nature of justice'. The 'psychology, linguistics or philosophy' claim, which the prior review asked to delete, is still there and not on the page.

fact_check.claim: BIO-AS: life from cells to ecosystems, including molecular makeup, evolution and genetic information
fact_check.note: Page text we could retrieve: 'Students learn to describe how organisms are connected to each other and to their physical environment' / 'understanding a wide range of life forms'. The cells/molecular/evolution/genetic list could not be found.

fact_check.claim: PHS-AS: physics, chemistry, Earth science, astronomy and scientific inquiry
fact_check.note: Page text: 'expose students to both the process and some of the substance of science' and 'appreciation of how science generates and categorizes enduring knowledge'. The subject list was not found.

fact_check.claim: SDS-AS covers statistical and computational methods for collecting, analyzing and interpreting data; SMR-AS covers abstract, logical and quantitative reasoning incl. mathematical modeling and algorithm design
fact_check.note: Page text: SDS 'develop data literacy, essential to be an informed citizen'; SMR 'help students develop the skills to solve problems'. Article's wording is not what we could find.

fact_check.claim: ALC-AS: creative expression and analysis of texts, artworks and belief systems
fact_check.note: Page text retrieved: 'examine arts, literature, and culture in various contexts' and 'analysis of artworks and literary texts'. 'Creative expression' and 'belief systems' could not be confirmed (fetcher returns only excerpts).

fact_check.claim: HST-AS: analysis of documentary, material and oral evidence
fact_check.note: Verbatim match.

fact_check.claim: Social Difference covers differences such as class, race and gender
fact_check.note: Page lists class, race, ethnicity, indigeneity, nationality, language, religion, gender among categories; the article's three are a subset.

fact_check.claim: Beyoncé Nation, taught by Riché Richardson, cross-listed in American Studies, Africana Studies, English and FGSS; recommended by a biology and society major; author calls it fun, makes distribution manageable; uses older name 'Literature and the Arts'; undated
fact_check.note: All confirmed (author Sheyla Finkner '19). Page has no visible date.

fact_check.claim: 2017 Cornell Daily Sun opinion column named Oceanography as an easy-A science route and cited a tour guide pitching a history of mathematics course as a math escape
fact_check.note: Published Sep 4, 2017; first-person opinion; mentions Oceanography 'easy A' and 'The History of Mathematics' per tour guide.

fact_check.claim: r/Cornell thread did not load
fact_check.note: Not relayed in the article; no fact depends on it.

beats_top.query: cornell arts and sciences easy distribution courses
beats_top.why: The #1 result is the official per-category course list, which is what the student ends up needing, and our page still offers almost no course picks (two dated leads) while paraphrasing category descriptions in ways the official page does not support.
changes: Replace the paraphrased category descriptions with the official wording and drop unsupported subject lists
Add sourced, current course examples per category, or reframe as a rules-and-process guide
Lead with the 8-course plan and the add/drop dates in the first paragraph
